'''John Newton Dodd''' (19 April 1922 – 20 May 2005) was a New Zealand physicist who worked in the field of [[atomic spectroscopy]].

==Early life and family==
Born in [[Hastings, New Zealand|Hastings]] in 1922,<ref name="RSNZ obit">{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/publications/reports/yearbooks/year2005/obituaries/john-dodd/ |title=John Newton Dodd |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |first=Rob |last=Ballagh |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref><ref name=JDDoddWalls>{{cite web|url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/dodd-walls/about/history/index.html|title=About Jack Dodd and Dan Walls|access-date=10 June 2018|archive-date=2 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202172449/https://www.otago.ac.nz/dodd-walls/about/history/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Dodd was educated at [[Otago Boys' High School]].<ref name="HBTQ">{{cite book |last1=Taylor |first1=Alister |last2=Coddington |first2=Deborah |author-link1=Alister Taylor |author-link2=Deborah Coddington |title=Honoured by the Queen – New Zealand |year=1994 |publisher=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa |location=Auckland |isbn=0-908578-34-2 |page=123}}</ref> In 1950, he married Jean Patricia Oldfield with whom he had four children.<ref name="HBTQ"/>

==Academic career==
Dodd attended the [[University of Otago]], graduating with a master's degree with first-class honours in 1946.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university7.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Da–Do |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> After earning his doctorate at the [[University of Birmingham]], he returned to the University of Otago to take up a lectureship in the [[Department_of_Physics_at_the_University_of_Otago|Department of Physics]]. He was awarded a professorial chair in 1965 and retired in 1988.<ref name="RSNZ obit"/>

While on leave in Oxford in 1959–1960, he worked with [[George Series]] who was applying techniques developed by [[Alfred Kastler]]'s research group in Paris to demonstrate that [[radiation]] from a coherent superposition of excited states of atoms would display interference effects, known as [[quantum beats]], and together they developed the theoretical explanation for the phenomenon.<ref name=qb2>{{cite journal|journal=Proceedings of the Physical Society|date=1959|pages=789–791|volume=74|issue=6|first1=J N|last1=Dodd|first3=G W|last3=Series|first2=W N|last2=Fox|first4=M J|last4=Taylor|title=Light Beats as Indicators of Structure in Atomic Energy Levels|doi=10.1088/0370-1328/74/6/122|bibcode=1959PPS....74..789D}}</ref><ref name=qb1>{{cite journal|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences|date=1961|pages=1314|volume=263|issue=1314|first1=J N|last1=Dodd|first2=G W|last2=Series|title=Theory of Modulation of Light in a Double Resonance Experiment|bibcode=1961RSPSA.263..353D|doi=10.1098/rspa.1961.0165|s2cid=122747243 }}</ref> His friendship with Series was long lasting, and it was Jack Dodd who edited a memorial Festschrift for George Series after his death in 1995.<ref name=DoddMemories>{{cite journal|journal=Physica Scripta|volume=T70|pages=5|first= J N|last=Dodd|date=1997|title=Editorial|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/1997/T70/E02|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Dodd was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1964,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/fellows-1919-present/d-f/ |title=The Academy: D–F |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> and was president of the society from 1989 to 1993.<ref name =PresRSNZ>{{Cite web | url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-council/presidents | title=Presidents}}</ref> In 1976, he won the society's [[Hector Memorial Medal|Hector Medal]], at that time the highest prize in New Zealand science.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/hector-medal/recipients/ |title=Hector Medal |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> In 1990, he was awarded the [[New Zealand 1990 Commemoration Medal]].<ref name="HBTQ"/>

==Honorific eponym==
The [[Dodd-Walls Centre|Dodd-Walls Centre for Photonic and Quantum Technologies]], a New Zealand Centre of Research excellence based in the University of Otago, was named after Jack Dodd and [[Dan Walls]] in recognition of their pioneering roles in establishing New Zealand's internationally recognised standing in photonics, quantum optics and ultra-cold atoms.<ref name=JDDoddWalls/>
